chunks: Part of the same sermon on the settlement between Mu'āwiyah and ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ : He did not swear allegiance till he got him agree that he would pay him its price.
The hand of this purchaser (of allegiance) may not be successful and the contract of the seller may face disgrace.
Now you should take up arms for war and arrange equipment for it.
Its flames have grown high and its brightness has increased.
Clothe yourself with patience for it is the best to victory.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the political settlement between Muawiya and Amr ibn al-As in Shia historical narrative?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha critiques the transactional nature of Mu'awiya's acquisition of power through Amr ibn al-As, framing it as a betrayal of political trust (amanah) that necessitated military readiness. It serves as a strategic exhortation to prepare for conflict, emphasizing that patience (sabr) is the most effective means to achieve victory, a theme deeply resonant in Shia historical narratives regarding the struggle against Umayyad authority.
